findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a reviewer cites a checkout through a symlinked absolute path.
The promised item is: "A review whose findings name files by an absolute path inside the checkout is kept, and those findings show the repo-relative path with no second review run." Git's worktree listing supplies `top` (`src/forge/story.py:822-824`), and on macOS it can return `/private/var/...` for a checkout also accessible as `/var/...`. Both source roots then use the former spelling, so the prefix comparison at `src/forge/review_process.py:116-119` leaves a `/var/...` citation absolute. The pinned validator rejects it (`tests/fixtures/autoreview-ce14dcca/scripts/autoreview:6811`), and `src/forge/review.py:997-1014` starts another review. The same comparison also rejects Windows citations whose root differs in case from both recorded spellings. The new test supplies only one spelling of `checkout`, so it does not cover either case.
findings.title: Not done: A review whose findings name files by an absolute path inside the checkout is kept, and those findings show the repo-relative path

why: A review finding that names a file by its absolute path makes the review helper discard the whole review, so its tokens (about 3M once) are wasted and the review runs again.
